# Spotlight

Spotlight: a one-step onboarding callout anchored to a `SpotlightTarget`, drawn on `Popover.Positioner` from `@base-ui/react`.

Also asked as: onboarding, feature tour, coach mark, new feature highlight, walkthrough.

**Import:** `import { Spotlight } from '@/components';`

**Source:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Spotlight/Spotlight.jsx`

**Stories:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Spotlight/Spotlight.stories.jsx` — Basic, WithMedia, LinkAction, PrimaryAction, SecondaryAction, Interactive, Rest, Hovered, Pressed, Focused

**Storybook page:** `design-system/src/components/messaging/Spotlight/Spotlight.mdx`

## Usage

Use `Spotlight` to call out one feature the first time someone can use it:
a new button, a changed control, a place to start. It is a single step or a
short, explicit sequence with a `stepCount`, not an ongoing help system.

For a message that stays on the page until resolved, use `SectionMessage` or
`Banner` instead. For a short note tied to one field or value, use
`InlineMessage`.

## Content guidelines

| Do | Don't |
| --- | --- |
| Name the feature in the headline: "Create a new board". | Write a headline that only says "New". |
| Use one or two short lines in the body. | Explain the whole feature. |
| Label actions with verbs: "Next", "Skip", "Got it". | Use "OK" for every step. |

## Best practices

### Name the feature, then say what to do. {#name-the-feature-then-say-what-to-do}

A headline names the thing; the body is one sentence.

Do: Short headline, one-sentence body.
Don't: A greeting and a paragraph.

### Show a step count only in a tour. {#show-a-step-count-only-in-a-tour}

One step alone has nothing to count.

Do: 1 of 3 in a three-step tour.
Don't: 1 of 1 on a single tip.

### Make the secondary action a link. {#make-the-secondary-action-a-link}

The primary action leads; the second one stays quiet. A `SpotlightAction` with
`href` renders as a link.

Do: Secondary action as a link.
Don't: Two competing buttons.

### Wrap the target and the callout in one SpotlightProvider. {#wrap-the-target-and-the-callout-in-one-spotlightprovider}

`SpotlightTarget` and `Spotlight` share an anchor through context, so both
need to sit inside the same provider. Pass `target` directly only when the
anchor comes from outside that tree.

```jsx
<SpotlightProvider>
    <SpotlightTarget>
        <Button text="Create" />
    </SpotlightTarget>
    <Spotlight headline="Create a new board" onDismiss={() => setSeen(true)}>
        Start a new board from here.
    </Spotlight>
</SpotlightProvider>
```

### Dismiss it once, and remember that it was seen. {#dismiss-it-once-and-remember-that-it-was-seen}

`isOpen` is yours to control. Store whatever "seen" state applies, such as a
user preference or a session flag, so the same spotlight does not reopen on
every visit.

## Accessibility

- **A dialog, not a tooltip.** The callout is a popover with a title and a
  description, read together when it opens.
- **The dismiss control is the first focusable element.** Tab reaches it
  before the body or the actions, so closing never requires finding the
  target again.
- **Escape closes it.** Dismissing with Escape or the close button calls
  `onDismiss`.
